clue.text: Nosy types take detective to corpses

parts.note: a busy is old slang for a police detective
corpses are dead bodies

explanation.surface: Interfering people bring a detective along to view dead bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSY is old British slang for a detective; 'take ... to' merely joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Meddlers who poke into other people's affairs are nosy types.

clue.text: Stole, grabbing high explosive something like gunpowder?

indicators.note: the stole holds the explosive in its grip, so it goes inside

parts.note: a boa is a long feathery scarf or stole

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a stole around explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunpowder is a Chinese green tea; Bohea is a black tea, so the two are alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Chinese teas, one black and one green.

clue.text: Deputy carrying round gun in county coming to premature end

indicators.note: the shortened county name holds the other pieces within it
the county's name is stopped before its final letter

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London
o is round in shape
a gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A stand-in brings a gun into a county where someone dies young.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY, an English county, loses its last letter to SURRE, which holds O and GAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute acting in place of another is a deputy.

clue.text: Mixed bathing run very much for larks?

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: r is the abbreviation for run in cricket scores
dearly means very much, as in loving dearly

explanation.surface: Mixed bathing that's tremendously good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges BATHING plus R into BRIGHTAN; 'larks' suggests fun, but these are birds that rise at dawn, like early risers.
explanation.definitionFit: Early risers are called larks, and they are up first thing in the morning.

clue.text: Condescends to bring in son's sketches

indicators.note: the verb for condescending takes in the son's letter

parts.note: deigns means condescends
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone condescends to let a son show his drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or drawings are sketches.

clue.text: A1's a road of France going over the whole continent

indicators.note: in a down clue going over turns the pieces upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: the A1 is a major British road, AI in letters, with S from the 's
rue is French for street or road

explanation.surface: Britain's A1 and a French road taken together span a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh; 'going over' reverses the whole AISARUE string.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe and Asia together form one landmass, a single continent.

clue.text: Talking bird

definitions.meaning: chatting is talking, as a noun: an informal conversation
a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.definitionFit: Both a casual conversation and a small thrush-like songbird share this word.

clue.text: Farmworker's current language

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A farmhand's present way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The main official tongue of northern India is a language.

clue.text: Its winner was given a personal column

definitions.text: Its winner was given a personal column

parts.words: Its winner was given a personal column
parts.note: Nelson won the 1805 naval battle and stands atop his own column in London

explanation.surface: Reads like a newspaper columnist being rewarded with a regular slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Personal column suggests newspaper small ads; it is Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson won this sea battle and was honoured with a monument.

clue.text: Bird unable to fly — sovereign's swan on snare around start of upping

parts.note: an emperor is a sovereign
a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: the snare surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: a gin is a trap or snare

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A monarch's swan is caught in a trap at the start of swan-upping.
explanation.walkthrough: Swan upping is the annual census of the Thames swans owned by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Antarctic species is a flightless seabird.

clue.text: County split by motorway? Solitude's what they want

indicators.note: the county name is cut open so the motorway can sit in its middle

parts.note: Herts is the short form of Hertfordshire, an English county
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in letters

explanation.surface: A rural county is carved up by a new motorway, and some residents just want peace.
explanation.walkthrough: HERTS is Hertfordshire, a county north of London; the M1 motorway runs through it, so MI goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Recluses living apart from society are people who seek solitude.

clue.text: Does it show great enthusiasm being next to central Europe?

definitions.text: Does it show great enthusiasm being next to central Europe?

parts.words: Does it show great enthusiasm being next to central Europe?
parts.note: the country's name ends in a word for great enthusiasm, a craze, and the land borders central Europe on its eastern side

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether a neighbour of central Europe is wildly keen.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters spell MANIA, great enthusiasm; the country lies just beyond central Europe, by the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan state bordering Hungary sits right beside central Europe.

clue.text: Prize man got in annual gatherings for pithy pronouncements

indicators.note: the two short pieces are brought inside the meetings, as if admitted

parts.note: AGMs are annual general meetings
a pot is a sporting trophy or prize
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A trophy winner gets admitted to yearly meetings where people trade wise sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Short witty maxims or aphorisms are terse, pithy sayings.

clue.text: Flower-dealer naturally speaking badly of rain and hurricanes

definitions.text: Flower-dealer naturally speaking badly of rain and hurricanes

parts.words: Flower-dealer naturally speaking badly of rain and hurricanes
parts.note: the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, drilled on 'the rain in Spain' and 'hurricanes hardly ever happen', which she naturally mangles

explanation.surface: A street florist grumbles about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle sells flowers in Shaw's play; her elocution lessons use phrases about rain and hurricanes, which she at first pronounces badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolittle is the flower seller of Pygmalion who learns to speak properly.

clue.text: Climber puts a spike back

indicators.note: the short phrase built from the article and the spike is read from right to left

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A mountaineer hammers a spike back into the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A NAIL around as a whole, giving the vine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical woody vine that climbs up trees is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Electrical apparatus producing field to study shock

parts.note: a ley is grassland or a field
a den is a private study
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A device that produces a field to examine electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: An early capacitor storing static charge is a piece of electrical apparatus.

clue.text: Observing as tail from fish still to be coughed up

parts.note: the shad is a herring-like fish
money still to be paid is owing; to cough up is to pay

explanation.surface: Someone tails a fishmonger whose bill remains unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Following someone secretly to watch them is tailing them.

clue.text: Not reacting about most of treasure person turned in

indicators.note: the unreactive word goes about the trimmed treasure

parts.note: inert means not reacting chemically

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for treasure is dropped

parts.note: trove is found treasure, as in treasure trove

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by a treasure that's been handed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned in' looks like handing in the treasure, but it means turned inwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose attention is directed inwards is a shy, reserved type.

clue.text: Bailey led astray, being submissive

indicators.note: letters led astray wander from their order into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Bailey is led off course and meekly gives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to give way or comply readily is submissive.

clue.text: Biographer to cry up favourably

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to sob is to cry
well means favourably

explanation.surface: A writer praises a subject warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell wrote the famous life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson, so he is a biographer.

clue.text: Put name on document, perhaps necessary to present it legally

indicators.note: the answer is a part necessary to the phrase, contained within it

explanation.surface: Signing a document may be required for it to be presented in law.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across presENT IT LEgally.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a title to something, such as a document, is to name it.

clue.text: What's wife removed from metal alloy safe?

indicators.note: the letter for wife is taken out of the alloy's name

parts.note: pewter is an alloy chiefly of tin

explanation.surface: A question about what remains when a wife is taken out of a tin alloy.
explanation.walkthrough: A peter is old criminal slang for a safe, the kind a safecracker blows.
explanation.definitionFit: In thieves' slang a strongbox or safe is called this.

clue.text: More insignificant actor in film

definitions.meaning: a walk-on background performer in a movie crowd scene

explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional, and also a non-speaking film performer in the background.

clue.text: I live in dry country

indicators.note: the two pieces sit inside the abstaining letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a teetotal land.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan region, often called a nation, is a country.

clue.text: Timber I do not saw freely

indicators.note: the letters are free to move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A carpenter declares he never cuts his wood loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard yellowish wood used in fine furniture is a timber.

clue.text: Eater gutted after row in cheap restaurant

indicators.note: the gutted eater is placed after the noise

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: a gutted word loses its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gutted customer after a quarrel in a greasy spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: A diner is an American-style cheap restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: An inexpensive roadside eatery serving simple meals is a cheap restaurant.

clue.text: Bad temper for third of June anniversary?

indicators.note: the bad temper takes the place of the third letter of the month

parts.note: the month's name taken as written
bile is irritability or bad temper

explanation.surface: Bad temper replacing June's festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of June' names the N, which gives way to BILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A special anniversary celebration, such as a monarch's 25th or 50th year, takes this name.

clue.text: One being delivered soon after Mayday

definitions.text: One being delivered soon after Mayday

parts.words: One being delivered soon after Mayday
parts.note: a baby born in early May, under the zodiac sign of the Bull, rather than a distress call

explanation.surface: A rescue arrives shortly after a distress signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayday suggests the distress call, but it is just 1 May; someone born then is under the Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born between late April and late May falls under Taurus.

clue.text: Verity's put out head girl

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dismissed from it

parts.note: verity is truth; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Verity has dismissed the head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Verity looks like a girl's name, but it is the word for truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, borne by the biblical Moabite woman.

clue.text: Source of current change by alliance? Right

parts.note: to alter is to change
NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance

explanation.surface: Asking whether altering an alliance is the right move.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator producing alternating electric current is a source of current.
